description: Codespaces but open-source, client-only and unopinionated: Works with any IDE and lets you use any cloud, kubernetes or just localhost docker.

summary.one_liner: DevPod is an open-source, client-only tool that creates reproducible developer environments from a devcontainer.json on backends such as the local machine, Kubernetes, remote machines, or cloud VMs.
summary.what_it_does: DevPod runs each developer environment in a container specified by a devcontainer.json file. Providers determine where the environment is created, including the local computer, a Kubernetes cluster, any reachable remote machine, or a cloud VM. Every workspace is managed the same way, so switching between workspaces hosted in different places is straightforward. It connects a local IDE to the remote environment, with VSCode and the JetBrains suite supported and other IDEs reachable over plain SSH. The README says DevPod already supports prebuilds, automatic shutdown after inactivity, and git and Docker credential sync. It offers a desktop app and a CLI.
use_cases: Creating reproducible development environments from devcontainer.json
Running dev containers on a cloud VM to save money
Developing locally with the same setup as a cloud workspace
Using a GPU or powerful remote machine for development
Connecting JetBrains or other IDEs to a remote container over SSH
how_to_run: Download DevPod Desktop from the links in the README (macOS Silicon/ARM, macOS Intel/AMD, Windows, or Linux AppImage)
See the DevPod documentation for more information
notable: Client-only: no server backend to install; runs only on the user's computer
Provider model lets the same workflow run on local Docker, Kubernetes, remote machines, or cloud VMs
Uses the open DevContainer standard also used by GitHub Codespaces and VSCode DevContainers
Automatic shutdown of unused virtual machines to reduce cost
Offers both a desktop app and a feature-rich CLI
caveats: The README only lists desktop download links for macOS, Windows, and Linux AppImage; it gives no CLI install steps
Cost savings claim (5-10x cheaper than hosted services) is the project's own claim and is not independently verified in the README
Full setup details are deferred to external documentation
